chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the seven walled gardens (enclosures) which were the legacy of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) for Fatima (peace be upon her). So he said: 'No, but rather they were a Waqf (endowment), and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to take from them whatever he spent on his guests, and the maintenance that was required for them. So when he passed away, Al-Abbas came disputing with Fatima (peace be upon her) regarding them. So Ali (peace be upon him) and others testified that they were a Waqf upon Fatima (peace be upon her), and they are: Al-Dallal, Al-Awaf, Al-Husna, Al-Safiya, what belonged to Umm Ibrahim, Al-Maysab, and Al-Burqa.'

ai.seo_question: What was the legal status of the seven gardens left to Fatima (peace be upon her)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that the seven walled gardens (Hitan) were not merely inherited property but constituted a Waqf dedicated to the Prophet's household and guests, a status contested by Al-Abbas after the Prophet's death. The narration highlights the pivotal role of Ali ibn Abi Talib and other companions in testifying to Fatima's exclusive right to these endowments, underscoring the distinction between personal inheritance and charitable endowment in early Shia jurisprudence. The specific names of the gardens, such as Al-Dalal and Al-Mithab, are preserved here, linking the material legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt to their spiritual and social authority.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the seven walls (walled gardens) which were a legacy of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> for Fatima<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘No, but rather these were dedicated (Waqf), and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to take from these whatever expenses there were upon for his<sup>saww</sup> guests, and the necessary maintenance of these. So when he<sup>saww</sup> passed away, Al-Abbas came over disputing with Fatima<sup>asws</sup> with regards to it. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> and others testified that these are dedicated (Waqf) over Fatima<sup>asws</sup>, and these were – Al-Dallalo, and Al-Awaaf, and al-Husna, and Al-Safiya, and what was for mother of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, and Al-Maysab, and Al Burqa’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Thani, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the seven walls (gardens) which were of the legacy of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, for Fatimah, Alayha al-Salam.

He (the Imam) said, ’No, they were endowments. The Messenger of Allah would take thereof for his guests and maintenance as needed. When he (the Messenger of Allah) passed away, al- ’Abbas came to dispute Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, about it. So she presented Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and others who testified that they were endowments and she, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was the beneficiary thereof. The gardens are called al-Dalal, al-‘Awaf, al-Husna’, al-Safiyah, Ma li ’Umm Ibrahim, al-Maythab and al-Burqah.’”
